title: Nvidia posts record results a week after Jensen Huang's resignation; board says he won't return
seoTitle: Nvidia after Jensen Huang: record quarter, SEC probe report
dek: Huang stepped down as CEO and chairman on 12 November. Nvidia then reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103%, and forecast about $130 billion assuming no data-centre chip sales to China. Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports an SEC probe.
happened: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder, stepped down as chief executive and board chairman on 12 November after 33 years. Scripps News reports that the New York Times had reported several extramarital affairs, including one with a former executive of a Singapore-based data-centre company whom US intelligence officials reportedly believe was a Chinese asset; that company has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. China denies she spied for it, Al Jazeera reports. Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation, and chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim CEO. On 17 November Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and above its own $108 billion guidance, with net income of $65.3 billion. It forecast about $130 billion for the next quarter, plus or minus 3%, assuming zero data-centre chip sales to China. TechCrunch reports the shares fell about 10% after Huang's departure and rose about 4% after hours on the results.

sides.says: New board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the earnings call: "The board does not intend to reinstate" Huang as CEO. He declined questions on the resignation or the investigation, saying the board "would communicate further when appropriate". The board has set up a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee and is considering internal and external candidates for CEO.

"From a business perspective, it's business as usual." She said: "We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap", and that suppliers and partners are "100% behind us".
He wrote on X: "I have made serious mistakes in my personal life." He said he would be "honored" to return as CEO if the board decided that was in shareholders' best interests.

President Trump told reporters, when asked about Huang returning: "I would not mind that." The Commerce Department moved the day before the results to close loopholes that let Chinese companies obtain advanced US AI chips through third countries or by renting computing power abroad. Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports that the Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia; the reports read here do not say what the probe covers.

next: Huang is scheduled to appear before three House committees (Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and the Select Committee on China) on 1 December, and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter on 2 December. The board has given no timeline for naming a permanent CEO.
summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO and chairman on 12 November after reports about his private life raised national-security questions, and the board says it will not reinstate him. Under interim CEO Colette Kress, Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and forecast about $130 billion, assuming no data-centre chip sales to China. Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports an SEC probe, and Huang is due before House committees on 1 December.
